title: Final kinetic energy
description: Essential Criteria: The student's final numerical answer for part (1) must be approximately 9.7 × 10⁻¹⁸ J.

title: Final potential difference
description: Essential Criteria: The student's final numerical answer for part (2) must be approximately 15.2 V.

title: Velocity decomposition
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly relate the final speed to the initial speed using the given 30° angle, typically via v = v₀ / cos 30°.

title: Work-energy application
description: Important Criteria: The student must apply the work-energy theorem, stating that the work done by the electric field equals the change in kinetic energy.

title: Correct formula substitution
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly substitute the electron's mass, charge, and velocities into the kinetic energy and work-energy formulas.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The student's working should demonstrate consistent use of SI units (kg, m/s, C, J, V) throughout the calculation.

title: Sign error for electron
description: Pitfall Criteria: The student incorrectly uses a positive sign for the electron's charge in the potential difference calculation, leading to a negative voltage.

title: Incorrect angle relation
description: Pitfall Criteria: The student mistakenly uses sine or tangent of the 30° angle to find the final speed, e.g., v = v₀ / sin 30°.
